who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), executor, int-1112 expect track
what: `#[blaze::may(alloc)]` on a function proved not to allocate passed for any public function and only warned (`unneeded_effect`) on a private one, so a list read as a promise said nothing: a reader could not tell from `may(alloc)` whether the function allocates.
cost: effect lists in the tree drifted from what the code does; the owner had to ask for the rename
cause: one spelling stood for two meanings, a bound on others (trait methods, defaults) and a statement about this body, and the checker took the weaker meaning for both
class: one annotation carrying a bound and a claim, checked only as the bound
prevention: `blaze::expect` on a function with a body and its own list is exact (`unfulfilled_effect`, deny); inherited, trusted, bodiless and unknown lists stay bounds; `Marks.exact` is the one place that decides which
fix: may renamed expect and deleted (refused with a respelling fix); unneeded_effect removed and banned. Control: the PRIVATE_ONLY plant brings back the old private-only check and an_unfulfilled_word_is_refused_on_every_function_that_writes_its_list fails.
